title: Expressions and operators: grouping, values, and clear steps
goal: Compare two expressions and see how parentheses change grouping.

prerequisites.text: You know addition, multiplication and declarations.

sections.title: From the task to an operation
paragraphs: An expression computes a value: 2+3*4 produces a number. Multiplication has higher precedence: first 3*4=12, then 2+12=14. Parentheses explicitly group operations: (2+3)*4 gives 20.

Braces group statements into a block and limit local names. They do not replace arithmetic parentheses. Precedence defines grouping; it is not a general execution-order rule for all side effects. Avoid modifying one variable several times in a complex expression.

sections.title: When the result differs
paragraphs: Removing b’s parentheses changes 20 to 14; changing indentation does not.

paragraphs: Compute 10-2*3 and (10-2)*3. Name the first operation for each result.

selfcheck.prompt: Compute 10-2*3 and (10-2)*3. Name the first operation for each result.
selfcheck.feedback: Compare the output with the readable reference case below. Explain each change using the objects or operations in this topic. In 10-2*3, 2*3 runs first and the result is 4. In (10-2)*3, 10-2 gives 8 first, then the result is 24. Removing parentheses changes 24 to 4; indentation does not.

practice.title: Independent variation
practice.task: Compute 10-2*3 and (10-2)*3. Name the first operation for each result.
criteria: Compare the output with the readable reference case below.
Explain each change using the objects or operations in this topic.
In 10-2*3, 2*3 runs first and the result is 4. In (10-2)*3, 10-2 gives 8 first, then the result is 24. Removing parentheses changes 24 to 4; indentation does not.

terms.definition: A combination of operands and operations producing a typed value in our calculations.
A value or nested expression to which an operation applies.
A rule for grouping operators when parentheses are absent.
Grouping for operators at the same precedence level, not a general evaluation-order promise.
A named calculation result that can be observed and checked separately.
